correctness.rationale: Both norms depend only on the character order \(L\). For the positive trinomial, \(|1+z+z^2|=|1+2\cos\theta|\); the quartic \(q(x)=15/32+9x^2/16-x^4/32\) majorizes \(|x|\) on \([-1,3]\) by the two exact factorizations in the package. For \(L\ge5\), root-of-unity orthogonality gives mean \(x^2=3\) and mean \(x^4=19\), hence norm at most \(25/16\). For the signed trinomial, multiplication by \(z^{-1}\) gives magnitude \(\sqrt{1+4\sin^2\theta}\); concavity places this above its endpoint chord, and mean \(\sin^2\theta=1/2\) for every \(L\ge3\), giving the lower bound \((1+\sqrt5)/2\). The two bounds are strictly separated. Direct root-of-unity evaluation yields the \(L=3,4\) values. Fresh independent numerical evaluation for every \(3\le L\le1000\) reproduced strict reversal, while the algebraic inequalities provide the all-\(L\) proof.
correctness.risk: The constants for \(L\ge5\) are separating certificates, not claimed exact norms or an optimal uniform gap.
